findings.reason: as written the removal decision is not computable from the data the plan says it is taken on, so the node would either guess a substitute quantity or stall on a gate it cannot evaluate.
findings.text: the removal criterion requires "its cumulative input per landed node rises, or its landing rate falls, by a difference whose paired interval is separated from the same-arm spread … §14 measures", but §13 makes the replay run never land ("build and gate exactly like an implementation run and then never be reviewed, merged or landed"), so the population that carries the required paired interval has no landed node and its landing rate is structurally zero, while §14 pairs cumulative input with gate pass rate; the only population carrying the interval therefore cannot produce either named quantity

findings.reason: the node must choose one of two opposite writes to the flight defaults, and the choice changes what the plan's landing actually configures.
findings.text: the same Done-when tells the node that an unseparated treatment is "kept in place with its flight default unchanged" while also requiring "the flight default for `anchored_edit` per backend is set to what the verdict says", and §14 states an overlapping arm's "verdict under §8's rule is not adopt"; so one record is asked both to honour a do-not-adopt verdict in the defaults and to leave those defaults untouched

findings.reason: the endpoint is unreachable in one dispatch, so either the node reports a population that does not exist yet or a second record node has to be declared in the plan.
findings.text: the record is required to report "the pooled paired differences over every replayed section" after "the coordinator extends §14's paired replay with further landed sections", yet this section's node is dispatched once, only after every arm has its 30/15 runs, and nothing states a second dispatch of that record or which dispatch precedes the extension

response_events.note: s8 now reads the replay's own quantities: cumulative input tokens per run and gate pass rate, paired by section against the arm's baseline, stating that a replay never lands (s13). Landing rate and redispatch rate are reported for routed runs only and carry no verdict; the removal rule and the two-population check use the same two quantities.

The flight-default clause now follows the verdict in one direction: an adopted treatment's default is turned on, and every other treatment's default stays off, as before the section. A not-separated treatment is not adopted and stays in the code with its default off, so the two writes no longer conflict.
